synopsis: CDC metadata identifies the February 2022 NIOSH haul-truck fatality conference paper, SME preprint 22-085, as not peer reviewed, qualifying its evidentiary status in the accident discussion [f3071]. In the skeptic’s review, an undated NIOSH CDC page reports that HASARD detection distance at the operator cab’s “risk” threshold fell from about 18 inches to 5 inches as speed increased from 3 to 30 inches per second [f10657]. A separate undated archived CDC page describes NIOSH’s Intelligent Proximity Detection program as explicitly seeking better operator acceptance by reducing frustration from frequent false alarms and full stops [f10710]. Across these chapters, CDC-linked material supplies accident-source metadata, quantitative detection results, and an operator-acceptance objective, but the facts provide neither dates for the two program pages nor evidence that the acceptance objective was achieved [f3071, f10657, f10710].
